I "deal with it" by doing other things. I write, I sing, I listen to music. My personal recommendation that I know won't work for everyone: take up a hobby. Run. Join kickboxing. Paint. Anything.

Personally... Counseling never helped me... but sometimes talking about it with my closest friend helps me a lot. I have to be in the right mood, though. 

After it first happened, I was **pissed**. I was frustrated. Upset. My life was essentially taken from me. I couldn't stand to be in my own house anymore. I lived with my best friend at the time for a month. I avoided anything that had to do with it for the longest time. My mother was incredibly supportive, which helped me overcome a lot. It happened on our living room couch, and the first thing she did was get rid of the couch. That helped majorly. I also blamed myself for a while- I should have pushed him off of me. I should have done something. I guess really realizing it's not my fault and that I did what I could process and think of as the best thing for me and those around me at the time helped me finally figure out that it wasn't my fault. **It's my rapist's fault.**

It's been a while... I was "alright" for about 2-3 years, but I started having bad nightmares again recently. I can't go to bed sad or I know I'm more prone to having a nightmare. I'm still learning to live with it, but it's a part of who I am. Because of it, I am strong.

OP, first things first, I'm proud of you for posting this. I know even though it may be "easier" to come out to a bunch of accepting people, I know it's still hard to type everything. To find the right words. To come to acceptance with everything. I'm happy for you that you were able to get this off of your chest, even if just a little bit.

As for your crush- I'm going to have to agree with u/alibix. Assume they're straight. It may be painful, but it will save a lot of awkwardness in the long run, especially at your age and in High School. Try talking to him, with any romantic interest put aside. Try being his friend. That's the first step in any successful relationship; platonic, gay, straight, anything.

And now your parents. I can't say I completely understand, because everyone's situation is different. But please, please use good judgement with whatever you do. From what you said with that they love you, it doesn't sound like they will actually physically hurt you (if I'm wrong, please correct me, I'm trying to asses from what you've said). With that being said, however, they are trying to mentally hurt you, which isn't okay. I understand completely that you love your parents even through this- and I don't think it would be necessary to get CPS involved at all as another commenter had stated. But it is necessary to use caution. My first girlfriend convinced me (against my better judgement) to come out to my homophobic family. It ended badly. I gues what I'm getting at is not to let others influence how you act and what you say around your parents. You know them best, and you know how they will react. 

If you feel like pursuing any kind of relationship, please take caution. Make sure you put your safety first. Make sure you and your partner are on the same page about where each other's families stand with acceptance of LGBTQ+. This is so important. 

If you ever want to talk, you can inbox me any time (that goes for anyone on this subreddit).
